long_biography.plain_text:
Software executive Virendra Prasad was one of five inventors behind an Edifecs patent for translating medical codes. Their method matched codes through the medical concepts they represented, then used weighting and filtering to choose a translation. It addressed the difficulty of transferring records between systems whose coding categories did not correspond neatly.

He also coauthored research with University of Washington Tacoma scientists on predicting healthcare expenditure. The team tested machine-learning models against public claims and survey data, using patients' earlier medical histories and costs to estimate subsequent spending. The study compared several approaches, including regression trees and random forests.
